title: Apartment Home Lease Late Fee Assessment Rule
content:
Late fees on an Apartment Home Lease are charged only on rent. This rule states when rent is late, when late fees may be assessed, and the limits that apply to all late fees of one billing period. Several of its original clauses have been withdrawn; they are listed at the end, marked as no longer in force.

## Clauses in force

**1. Lease status.** Late fees may be assessed only while the lease is active or in default. The status is read from the lease record. No late fee is assessed once an eviction case is filed, and none is ever assessed on fees, utilities or other non-rent charges.

**2. When rent is late.** A billing period's rent is late on a day when the unpaid rent of that period, evaluated at the end of that day, is above 0.00. The unpaid rent of a period is the base rent and prorated rent charged for that period, less the rent concession, preferred employer discount and military discount credits for that period, less the part of every lease payment received by the end of that day (net of payment returns dated by then) that the payment allocation order assigns to that period's rent; it is never below 0.00.

**3. Earliest initial late fee.** An initial late fee may be assessed only when the frozen date is later than the rent due date of the billing period plus the effective grace period. The due date is read from the period's rent line on the ledger, and the community's state from the lease record. The comparison is strict: on the last day of the effective grace period itself, no initial late fee may yet be assessed.

**4. One initial late fee per period.** At most one initial late fee posts per billing period. The check is made against the initial late fee lines already on the ledger for the same lease and billing period.

**5. Period cap.** All late fees of one period together are capped at the lowest applicable cap. A fee that would pass the cap posts only the remaining room, and no line posts once the late fees of the period reach the cap. The late fees of a period are its initial and daily late fee lines less the courtesy waiver and charge reversal credits posted against those lines.

**6. Payment plans.** Periods covered by a signed payment plan in good standing accrue no late fees while the plan is in good standing.

### Illustrations of the clauses in force (hypothetical)

- A period whose rent line was fully offset by credits and payments by the end of a day is not late on that day, whatever its fee lines show.
- A cap with $40.00 of room left and a daily fee of $50.00 about to post: the line posts at $40.00, and after it nothing further posts for that period.
- A lease whose eviction case was filed on the 12th accrues no late fee on the 13th or after.

## Clauses no longer in force

The following original clauses of this rule have been withdrawn and are no longer in force. They are reproduced so that an older ledger can be read, not to be applied.

- *Effective grace period (no longer in force).* The clause defining the effective grace period as the longer of the floor plan's grace period and the minimum late days of the community's state is no longer in force. The state minimum late days recorded with this rule are: California 0, Washington 5, Colorado 7, Texas 2, Georgia 0, Arizona 0.
- *Counting grace days (no longer in force).* The clause counting grace days as calendar days starting the day after the rent due date, without skipping weekends or holidays, with the first late day being the day after the last grace day, is no longer in force.
- *Initial late fee amount (no longer in force).* The clause posting one initial late fee on the first late day equal to the greater of the floor plan's flat component and its percentage of the monthly rent in force on the due date, rounded half up to the cent, is no longer in force.
- *Daily late fees (no longer in force).* The clause posting one daily late fee of the floor plan's daily amount for each later calendar day on which the rent is still late, up to the floor plan's maximum daily late fees for the period, is no longer in force.
- *Company and Texas caps (no longer in force).* The clause setting the company cap at the floor plan's cap percentage times the monthly rent and, in Texas, a cap of 0.10 (10 percent) times the monthly rent, is no longer in force.
- *Colorado cap (no longer in force).* The clause setting, in Colorado, a cap at the greater of $50.00 and 0.05 (5 percent) times the rent unpaid on the first late day is no longer in force.
